summary: Phase 1C Turn C — Personalised contract issuance. Ran the main-agent-authored /app/backend/tests/test_phase1c_turn_c.py (21 tests: 10 render-engine unit + 11 integration against the live preview backend). ALL 21 pass on first run. Coverage confirmed for: hyperlink LINK_URI annotation shape + underline stroke; strict-overflow/missing-value/residual-token hard-fails in issuance mode; preview-mode lenient behaviour + watermark preserved; source_bytes immutability; full end-to-end issuance flow (draft → freeze-territory → resolve-variables → /issue) producing personalised.pdf under contract-issuances/{cid}/personalised.pdf with sha256/byte_size/created_at; signed-URL download SHA-match; clickable link uri matches frozen_territory_map_url on the contract; zero residual [[ tokens + no 'PREVIEW' watermark on issued PDF; source_pdf sha unchanged after issue; second /issue returns 409; audit trail carries contract.draft.create + contract.freeze_territory + contract.variables.resolve + contract.pending_issue + contract.issued (with r2_key + hyperlink_count + residual_token_count in extra); supersede flow flips predecessor to 'superseded' + emits contract.superseded audit event; Paloma template evidence-pack regression still returns valid ZIP. Added complementary suite /app/backend/tests/test_phase1c_turn_c_complement.py (7 additional tests, all pass) closing gaps: (a) evidence-pack ZIP is openable + contains a PDF artefact, (b) Paloma sample-preview.pdf still returns 200 with X-Preview-Redaction-Verified=1 + X-Preview-Residual-Tokens=0, (c) Paloma per-marker sample-preview.png still returns 200 with X-Overflow header, (d) render_report_summary shape on issued contract carries hyperlink_count=1 + link_annotations list of {page,uri,rect} + redaction_verified=true + template_version + source_pdf_sha256 (64 hex), (e) frozen_territory_map_url starts with 'https://hub.creativemojo.co.uk/agreed-territory/', (f) signed-URL HEAD/GET reveals Content-Type=application/pdf + Cache-Control includes 'no-store' or 'private', (g) double-issue does not change personalised_pdf_sha256 (immutability at the DB row level). Combined Phase 1C Turn A + B + C + all regression suites (test_phase1b_turn_a/b/c5_and_d, test_stop_point_3_manifest, test_auto_whitespace_expansion, test_address_and_overflow, test_bbox_split_redaction, test_contract_markers_pipeline, test_phase1c_turn_a/_complement, test_phase1c_turn_b/_complement, test_phase1c_turn_c/_complement): 201 passed / 1 documented skip / 0 failed in 48s. Paloma template c12c8ce1-…-fa23 still status='draft' and untouched.
critical_code_review_comments: Rollback path in contract_issuance_routes._issue on engine.RenderError emits contract.issue.aborted and reverts status pending_issue → draft (verified by reading the handler; no live end-to-end test in this iteration because upload-marker-pipeline auto-sizes render_bbox from the source token, so it is non-trivial to author an OVER-flowing template via the admin upload endpoint — the strict-overflow behaviour itself is covered end-to-end at the engine layer via engine.RenderError). Consider exposing an internal /admin/contracts/{id}/issue-dry-run that lets QA/integration tests trigger the hard-fail branch without an admin uploading a bespoke overflow PDF each time.

No admin endpoint currently returns the R2 head_object metadata dict directly (contract-id / template-version / personalised-sha256 / issued-by keys). The signed-URL GET reveals Content-Type + Cache-Control but not the custom Metadata keys. If evidence-pack Turn E is to prove those keys were set at upload time, add a lightweight /admin/contracts/{id}/personalised-pdf/metadata endpoint that returns fs.head_object(r2_key)['Metadata'].

render_report_summary.link_annotations stores rect as a raw tuple/list from PyMuPDF; document the tuple order (x0,y0,x1,y1) in a comment so downstream JSON consumers don't guess (the field is now durable on the contract row).

TestIssuancePreconditions.test_issue_refuses_on_missing_marker_value in the main-agent suite currently issues cleanly rather than forcing drift — it exercises the happy path a second time (comment on L466 acknowledges this). The 'missing values map' hard-fail path is only covered by the unit-level render engine test. Consider a dedicated integration test that mutates contract_variables via Mongo directly to drop one code, then asserts /issue → 409 with missing_codes populated (currently uncovered end-to-end).

Paloma template c12c8ce1-423b-4667-b5f7-da897546fa23 is NEVER mutated (evidence-pack + sample-preview + per-marker PNG are all read-only).
